**TERRA – Planetary Analogue Explorer**

TERRA is a planetary exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It focuses on identifying and exploring locations on Earth that share environmental and geological characteristics with the Moon and Mars.

The project addresses the challenge by helping users discover Earth-based planetary analogue environments, such as deserts, impact craters, volcanic landscapes, and polar regions. These locations can offer valuable insights into the conditions, terrain, and environmental challenges that may be encountered during future lunar and Martian exploration.

TERRA aims to make planetary analogue research more accessible by bringing relevant locations and information together in one interactive experience. By connecting Earth's diverse landscapes with the environments of other worlds, the project supports exploration, research, and a better understanding of potential locations for future space missions.

**Explore Earth. Prepare for other worlds.**
details:
TERRA — Planetary Analogue Explorer

TERRA is a web-based planetary analogue exploration platform designed to help users discover and compare Earth environments that share characteristics with locations on the Moon and Mars. Since studying other planetary surfaces directly is challenging, Earth environments with similar terrain and environmental conditions can provide useful reference points for research, education, and exploration planning.

The platform allows users to explore Earth locations and examine their potential similarities to lunar and Martian environments. TERRA focuses on factors such as terrain slope, surface roughness, and temperature context. It uses planetary and Earth observation resources to support exploration and comparison, helping users understand why certain Earth environments may be relevant analogues for other worlds.

Benefits and Intended Impact

TERRA makes planetary analogue exploration more accessible through an interactive and visual experience. It can help students, educators, space enthusiasts, and researchers explore the relationship between Earth's landscapes and planetary environments. By bringing relevant information and comparisons into one platform, TERRA aims to encourage scientific curiosity and make complex planetary exploration concepts easier to understand.

Tools, Technologies, and Data Resources

We developed TERRA as a web-based prototype using modern web development tools and technologies. Our project references several publicly available scientific resources, including:

  • LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter): Lunar elevation, slope, and roughness reference data.
  • LRO Diviner: Lunar surface temperature observations.
  • Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and NASADEM: Earth elevation data.
  • NASA Worldview / GIBS and Moon Trek: Planetary imagery, maps, and visual context.

These resources inform the project's exploration and comparison approach. The current prototype includes demonstration values and incomplete data coverage; its rankings are illustrative rather than scientifically validated. Temperature is treated as contextual information, not as part of the default comparison score.

Creativity and Design Approach

The creative aspect of TERRA is its attempt to connect familiar Earth landscapes with the challenges of exploring other planetary worlds. Instead of presenting planetary data as isolated scientific information, TERRA brings exploration, visualization, and comparison together in an accessible interface. The platform is designed to make users think beyond Earth's landscapes and understand how our planet can help us prepare for future exploration of the Moon and Mars.

Factors Considered

Our team considered terrain characteristics, environmental conditions, the availability and reliability of public scientific datasets, data coverage, and the limitations of comparing different planetary environments. We also prioritized usability and clarity so that users can explore the concept without needing advanced scientific knowledge.

TERRA is an initial prototype with room for further development, including improved dataset integration, more complete measurements, and scientifically validated comparison methods. Our long-term goal is to make planetary analogue discovery more informative, accessible, and useful for future exploration.
